title: Verify the Claude Code plugin in a real session with --plugin-dir
body: In a scratch git project that holds a `.dd/config.json` (and memories to try), run `claude -p "<prompt>" --plugin-dir <this checkout> --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events < /dev/null` and read the JSONL: the hook_response events carry what DD injected (hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext) and the assistant text is the agent's work; plain text output shows only the reply to DD's Stop request. The session's ledger and footprint land in `<scratch>/.dd/local/sessions/`. Why: --plugin-dir loads hooks/hooks.json exactly as a marketplace install does, for that run only, so the checkout is tested rather than the installed copy; src/eval/agent/run.js drives the same flags for the trials. A probe in a scratch project without a `.dd/` folder records nothing: the folder is the opt-in.
not_derivable: No test can run Claude Code; the flags, the event the injection appears in and the opt-in trap were found by running it.
